title: Remove the tree supports from a 3D-printed robot part, holding it over a scrap bin
instruction: Take the orange print off the printer, remove all of its supports into the white bin, and put the part in the blue tray.
context: Robot labs print their own linkages and brackets, and many have overhangs that cannot print without supports. This crank link from a gripper's linkage is one: its upper boss stands on the far end of a bar 25 mm above the bed, so the bar and the boss's rim need supports in any orientation (on its side, the bosses overhang). Before the part can be fitted, every support has to come off. Slicer tree supports touch the part only at 0.8 mm tips and are removed by hand: hold the part, take each support near its foot and bend it about its tips until they let go, over a scrap bin. Unlike snapping a scored panel over a fixed edge, there is no fixture: one hand holds a small part in the air while the other breaks off supports on different sides, and the part must be turned to reach the one hidden behind its raised boss. It follows popping the part off the build plate, so a robot that does both turns printer output into finished robot parts without a person: part of robots building robots.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table: x forward (away from the robot), y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Fixed: an open-frame 3D printer (Creality Ender-3, the manufacturer's CAD; black aluminium frame, 44 x 44 x 61 cm) at the far middle of the bench, its heated bed (23.5 x 23.5 cm, black textured build sheet, top 10.35 cm up) slid fully forward with its centre at (24, 0), its print head parked 10 cm above the bed, behind it. On the bed, loose, 4 cm in front of the bed's centre: the print, an orange PLA crank link (25 g, 20% infill): two bosses 28 mm across and 25 mm tall with 8 mm holes, 80 mm apart, joined by a 16 x 8 mm bar; it lies with the bar along y, the down boss on the bed at (20, +4), the bar 25 mm up on it, the up boss on top of the bar's far end at (20, -4) (the part stands 58 mm). Four orange PLA tree supports printed with it, standing on the bed: two under the bar (1.8 g each, 24.6 mm tall, trunks at (20, -3.5) and (20, 0), each splitting 20 mm up into six branches) and two under the up boss's overhanging rim (1.2 g each, 32.6 mm tall, trunks at (18.2, -4) and (21.8, -4), splitting 18 mm up into three branches); every branch ends in a 0.8 mm tip 0.2 mm under the part. Fixed: a white rigid-plastic open-top scrap bin, 9 x 9 x 5.5 cm, centred at (20, -17), on the table beside the printer's bed, in front of its display; a blue rigid-plastic open-top tray, 10 x 14 x 2.5 cm (long along y), centred at (16, -30). Both 3 mm walls.
scoring: A support is off once it has broken away from the part (its centre has moved more than 5 mm from its place, measured in the part's frame). A support is in the bin when its centre is inside the bin's walls and below its rim. The part is in the tray when its centre is inside the tray's walls and its lowest point rests on the tray's floor (within 1 cm). Score: 0.10 for each support that is off, plus 0.05 more for each of those that is in the bin (0.60 for all four in the bin), plus 0.40 if the part is in the tray with all four supports off; a part in the tray with any support still on earns nothing for the tray. Score 0 for the rest of the trial once the part falls off the table, falls freely (moves down faster than 1.4 m/s, the speed of a 10 cm drop), or lands in the bin. Success (1.0) also needs the part and supports still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s and both grippers more than 2 cm from the part. Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: The supports are consumed: print a fresh part for each trial from assets/crank_with_supports.stl (the part with these four tree supports modelled in, tips 0.2 mm under it) in PLA, 0.2 mm layers, 20% infill, with the slicer's own supports turned off, so a real trial has exactly the simulation's supports; print a batch ahead of a session. Print it on the Ender-3, let it cool and pop it free of the textured sheet (flex the sheet), then set it back loose on the bed at the position in the setup, bed slid fully forward, Z raised 10 cm. The break thresholds are estimates; the README gives the procedure to measure them on real prints. In simulation, run with -E object_jitter=0.
fidelity: Approximate: the part and each support are rigid bodies with their real shapes (cylinders and bar; a trunk and slim boxes along each branch), each support held to the part by a joint that breaks above an estimated 0.10 N m bend or 15 N pull (README: how to measure them), standing in for its 0.8 mm tips; real tips crumble and leave nubs. The printer is the manufacturer's CAD, fixed, colliding as boxes. One rubber-like friction on every contact (static 1.2, dynamic 1.0).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.15 (one support broken off into the bin); demo: 1.0 (in two runs out of two with the final code)
